facts.text: The README describes the repository as a UR5 pick-and-place demonstration in ROS and Gazebo using a USB camera and vacuum grippers.
The README says the default ur_description files include no camera or vacuum gripper modules and tells the user to copy the clone's common.gazebo.xacro and ur5.urdf.xacro over them.

The initialization launch starts Gazebo, uploads the robot description from the ur_description package, starts the UR5 arm controller and MoveIt, then starts the blocks_spawner, blocks_poses_publisher, ur5_vision, ur5_mp and ur5_gripper nodes.
The launch loads the arm controller from the ur_gazebo package and remaps /follow_joint_trajectory to /arm_controller/follow_joint_trajectory when sim is true.
The URDF declares the libgazebo_ros_vacuum_gripper.so plugin for the first gripper with robotNamespace /ur5/vacuum_gripper and topicName grasping.
The URDF declares further vacuum-gripper plugins under /ur5/vacuum_gripper1 through /ur5/vacuum_gripper8; the channel-3 plugin also names its topic grasping2.
The first vacuum plugin config sets maxForce 50, maxDistance 0.05 and minDistance 0.01.
The gripper node waits for the absolute /ur5/vacuum_gripper/on service and calls it with an Empty service proxy.
The gripper node waits for the absolute /ur5/vacuum_gripper/off service and calls it with an Empty service proxy.
The gripper node defines on and off functions for the eight additional channels, each naming /ur5/vacuum_gripperN/on or /ur5/vacuum_gripperN/off.
The gripper node imports Empty from std_srvs.srv and Bool from std_msgs.msg.
The gripper node subscribes to /ur5/vacuum_gripper/grasping with the Bool type.
The trigger callback calls every gripper on function when msg.flag2 is true and every off function otherwise.
The gripper node subscribes trigger to the relative cxy1 Tracker topic.
The vision node subscribes to /ur5/usbcam/image_raw with the Image type and publishes the relative topic cxy with the Tracker type.
The motion node subscribes to the relative cxy Tracker topic and publishes the relative cxy1 Tracker topic.
The motion node constructs MoveGroupCommander('manipulator') and executes plans through the MoveIt client.
The motion node registers cleanup with rospy.on_shutdown.
cleanup calls self.arm.stop() and shuts down MoveIt.
The motion node publishes the tracker with cxy_pub with flag2 1 when len(self.pointx) is 11, and with flag2 0 after it has executed the lift, transition, end-state and retreat plans.
The motion node's header states that the program is distributed under the GNU General Public License, version 2 or later.
The Tracker message declares float64 x, y, z, error_x, error_y and error_z and bool flag1, flag2 and flag3.
The block-pose node subscribes to /current_blocks and /gazebo/model_states and advertises the relative blocks_poses topic with the ur5_notebook/blocks_poses type.
The blocks_poses message declares float64 arrays x, y and z.
The camera plugin declares cameraName ur5/usbcam and imageTopicName image_raw with an 800 by 800 R8G8B8 image at 30 Hz.
The package manifest leaves the license field as TODO.
The initialization launch includes gazebo_ros's empty_world.launch with the world worlds/empty.world and paused and gui arguments that default to false and true.
The vacuum gripper plugin advertises its grasping Bool topic and its on and off std_srvs::Empty services on a custom callback queue.
The vacuum gripper plugin serves that queue on its own thread and connects UpdateChild to the world-update begin event.
The on service sets the stored status to true and the off service sets it to false.

UpdateChild publishes grasping false when the status is off; when it is on it pulls every link within 0.05 m of the gripper link with a force of at most 20 and publishes grasping true for such a link.
The vacuum plugin's queue thread serves its callbacks with a 0.01 s wall-clock wait while its node handle is ok.
gazebo_ros_control connects its Update to the world-update begin event.
gazebo_ros_control's Update reads the simulation time, updates the controllers and writes their commands to the simulated joints.
The gazebo_ros gzserver wrapper adds libgazebo_ros_api_plugin to the server's plugins unless the arguments already name it.
empty_world.launch starts the Gazebo server as the node named gazebo of package gazebo_ros, with the physics engine argument -e $(arg physics).
empty_world.launch defaults its physics argument to ode.
empty_world.launch defaults its gui argument to true.
When gui is true, empty_world.launch starts the node gazebo_gui of type gzclient.
The API plugin calls ros::init with the node name gazebo when ROS is not initialised yet.
The API plugin creates its node handle in the private namespace ~ and advertises its topics and services there.
The API plugin advertises the service pause_physics with the std_srvs::Empty type on its own callback queue gazebo_queue_.
The API plugin advertises the service get_physics_properties with the gazebo_msgs::GetPhysicsProperties type on gazebo_queue_.
gazeboQueueThread serves gazebo_queue_ in a loop with a 0.001 s wall-clock wait while the node handle is ok.
pausePhysics calls world_->SetPaused(true) and returns true.
unpausePhysics calls world_->SetPaused(false) and returns true.
getPhysicsProperties sets res.pause to world_->IsPaused().
getPhysicsProperties sets success true only when the physics engine type is ode; for any other engine it sets success false and returns false.
The GetPhysicsProperties response field pause is true if the physics engine is paused.
Among the world-update begin hooks that its comment says apply forces and publish sim time on /clock, the API plugin connects publishSimTime.
World::Step advances simulation time and calls Update only when the world is not paused, a step increment is pending or a reset is due; otherwise it adds the step to the pause time.
World::Step holds worldUpdateMutex while it steps the world.
World::SetPaused stores the paused flag under worldUpdateMutex.
World::IsPaused returns the stored paused flag.
World::Update fires the worldUpdateBegin event and then updates every model.
World::Step calls ProcessMessages after the paused or unpaused branch, so pending messages are processed on every step, paused or not.
A WorldControl message with step calls OnStep, and one with multi_step pauses the world and sets the number of steps to run while paused.

determinism.notes: Event-driven contract fake with no Gazebo physics, gripper attachment, MoveIt planner or wall-clock pacing; placeholder observations do not establish grasp or motion replay

gaps: the fake is a ROS-free analytic transport: it answers the declared services and subscriptions and runs no Gazebo, vacuum-gripper plugin, ODE physics, MoveIt, camera or wall-clock loop
the vacuum on/off handlers flip placeholder flags; the fake models no suction, contact, attachment, mass or object release, so a receipt does not prove a grasp
the grasping, cxy and blocks_poses values are placeholders; they do not establish a live perception or block state

the package exposes the nine vacuum on/off services, the first grasping topic, the cxy tracker topic and the blocks_poses topic; the UR5 arm motion through MoveIt and the trajectory controller, the camera image stream, block spawning, the Gazebo model services and the remaining gripper grasping topics are NOT COVERED

the stop is the companion gazebo_ros world pause: the fake keeps a paused flag that /gazebo/pause_physics sets and /gazebo/get_physics_properties reports; it runs no Gazebo World::Step; the vacuum off services are not a stop (they release the payload and do not stop the arm)

no unpause is offered: on an unpause the arm controller resumes the MoveIt trajectory ur5_mp sent (gazebo_ros_control updates the controllers from the world update) and each vacuum channel acts with its stored status (gazebo_ros_vacuum_gripper.cpp:147-168, 172-230); the package cannot clear the trajectory and must not release the vacuum (the payload would drop), so the operator recovers outside MHS: stop or restart ur5_mp and MoveIt (rospy.on_shutdown runs self.arm.stop(), ur5_mp.py:57, 149-158), then press play in the Gazebo GUI or call rosservice call gazebo/unpause_physics

while paused the vacuum services still answer (the plugin's queue thread runs on the wall clock), so a vacuum command after the reset changes the stored status that acts on the next unpause; the grasping, cxy and blocks_poses topics come from world-update plugins and the camera, so they are silent while paused and those reads fail NOT_READY (the fake silences them while its flag is set); ur5_gripper.py still switches every channel on again whenever ur5_mp publishes flag2 true on cxy1 (ur5_gripper.py:208-237, ur5_mp.py:211-213)

a live world can be unpaused or stepped by the Gazebo GUI that empty_world.launch opens by default, by a WorldControl message or by any ROS client; MHS does not watch the flag after the e-stop (safety_status re-reads it only on request)
the read-back needs the ODE engine (empty_world.launch's default physics): with another engine get_physics_properties returns false and the e-stop stays unconfirmed with the latch held
the deployment's gazebo_ros and Gazebo must be the pinned 2.5.21 (Kinetic) and 7.16.1 releases the companion citations name; rosbridge cannot read their versions

the vacuum plugins and the camera exist only after the user copies the clone's src/ur_description xacro files over the installed universal_robot ur_description, which initialize.launch uploads (README.md:46-49, launch/initialize.launch:20-22); otherwise no vacuum service or grasping topic exists and every vacuum call or grasping read fails

the fake reports grasping as the first channel's on state and answers an Empty call with a non-empty rejection value; the upstream plugin reports a grasp only for an object in range and an Empty response has no fields, so those two fake paths exercise the package's predicates only
no real ROS graph, Gazebo, MoveIt, simulator or hardware was contacted; evidence is F0 contract_checked only

safe_state.description: The Gazebo world is paused and get_physics_properties read pause true back: no world update runs, so the arm controller, the vacuum plugins and the physics are frozen and each vacuum channel keeps its state; it is the paused flag, not a measured standstill. No unpause is offered: an operator stops ur5_mp and its MoveIt goal and unpauses outside MHS.
